h1:
Where to Stay in Surin?
12 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites!
heroSub: 12 hand-picked Surin hotels across every budget — from Hop Inn's spotless rooms near the City Pillar Shrine down to a resort from ฿470/night. Covering the main areas: the city centre, around the monument and market, near the train station, and out by Huay Saneng reservoir. From roughly ฿470–1,300/night.
introH2: 🐘 Why does choosing the right area in Surin matter?
introHtml: Surin is a compact town you mostly get around by car, but where you stay still shapes how easy the trip feels. The city centre — around the City Pillar Shrine, the Phraya Surin monument and the in-town market — is where it's easiest to walk to Isan food, temples and everyday shops, ideal if you want to explore on foot without driving much. Near the train and bus stations suits anyone arriving by rail or coach without a car: step off and walk to your room. The Robinson side and the out-of-town area near Huay Saneng reservoir are quieter with easy parking, best for drivers who'd rather stay away from the bustle. Many people book without checking the area and burn the day shuttling in and out of town, or arrive by train but pick an out-of-town stay and end up stuck. This guide rounds up 12 Surin hotels we've already reviewed across every tier — with real guest-review scores, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Surin has no metro; you get around by car, though the centre is small enough to explore the core areas on foot. Many stays in the city centre (around the City Pillar Shrine, the monument and the in-town market) are within walking distance of temples, markets and restaurants, good if you want to explore the town. Stays near the train station and the bus (BKS) terminal suit rail and coach travellers — step off and walk to your room, no onward ride. The Robinson side and the out-of-town area near Huay Saneng are far easier with a private or rental car, as they sit on the edge of town. One thing to plan for: during the Surin Elephant Round-up in mid-November, hotels across the whole town fill fast and rates rise sharply, so book weeks ahead. The areas in this guide: City Centre — temples, markets, food · Near the train/bus station — easy by public transport · Huay Saneng / out of town — quiet, easy parking.

entries.name: Hop Inn Surin
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.3 · 126 reviews (most in the guide) · cleanliness 9.6
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Poi Tang Ko Soi · near the City Pillar Shrine & market
tags: 📍 Walk to the City Pillar Shrine & market
entries.addr: 5 Poi Tang Ko Soi, Nai Mueang, Mueang Surin
entries.storyHtml: Hop Inn Surin takes the top score and the most reviews in this guide — 9.3 from 126 reviews, with cleanliness as high as 9.6. It's part of the Hop Inn chain, where every branch shares the same standard room: clean, simple, and reliably what you expect, no guesswork. Real guest reviews agree the rooms are spotless, beds comfy and air-con cold, with a location that's a walk from Wat Burapharam, the City Pillar Shrine and the in-town market. The trade-off: it's a rooms-only hotel — no breakfast, no pool. Best for budget travellers and anyone arriving by train.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: There's a market and local restaurants within walking distance, so breakfast and dinner are easy. Prices move within a few hundred baht, so book direct or compare sites for a better deal. Parking is free on a first-come basis, so arrive a little early when it's busy.
pros: Top score 9.3 · most reviews (126) · cleanliness 9.6
Chain-standard spotless rooms, comfy beds, cold air-con
Walk to Wat Burapharam, the City Pillar Shrine and the market
Free Wi-Fi and parking · ~1.3 km from the train station
cons: No breakfast or restaurant; you'll eat out nearby
No pool or spa · shower pressure a touch weak in some rooms

entries.name: The Wood Hotel
entries.badge: 🌿 Forest theme in a green garden
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Thesaban Bamrung Soi · city centre · walk to market
tags: 🌿 Tucked into a quiet green garden
🚲 Free bikes to ride into town
entries.addr: 9 Thesaban Bamrung Soi, Nai Mueang, Mueang Surin
entries.storyHtml: The Wood Hotel is a forest-and-nature-themed boutique that scores high among the boutiques — 9.2 from 72 reviews, ranked #2 in Surin's boutique/guesthouse category on TripAdvisor. Its draw is being tucked into a leafy garden set back from the main road, so it feels as quiet as a small resort while still being in the city centre. Opened in 2020, the rooms are still new and clean, there are free bikes to borrow into the in-town market, and the breakfast earns praise. Worth knowing: the beds are on the firm side, there's some night-time noise, and the hotel sits deep in a soi that's tricky to find first time.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a Double Room with a balcony over the garden — the spot guests like best. Borrow a free bike to ride into the in-town market. Set your map app before arriving, since the hotel is deep in Thesaban Bamrung Soi. Some periods need breakfast ordered the evening before, so flag it at check-in.
pros: Tucked into a green garden, quiet despite being central
New, clean, nicely styled nature-theme rooms, opened 2020
Free bikes and free private parking, EV charger
Praised breakfast · friendly, helpful staff
cons: Firm beds, some water-pump noise, thin-ish walls
Deep in a soi — hard to find on a first visit

entries.name: Slive Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Lak Mueang Rd · city centre · near the City Pillar Shrine
entries.addr: 169 Lak Mueang Rd, Nai Mueang, Mueang Surin
entries.storyHtml: Slive Hotel is a newer hotel guests praise most for cleanliness — 9.1 from 34 reviews, ranked #2 of 12 Surin hotels on TripAdvisor. Opened in 2017 on Lak Mueang Road, it's a few minutes' walk from the City Pillar Shrine. The standouts are kitchenettes in many rooms, a gym better-equipped than you'd expect, a rooftop sky garden, and a free 24-hour shuttle to the train station — very handy if you don't have a car. The catch: there's no pool, the building is compact, and hot-water pressure is uneven in some rooms.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Arriving by train or flying into Buriram? Request the free shuttle in advance — it genuinely saves on the fare. Want a kitchenette? Specify it when booking, as not every room has one. Head up to the rooftop in the evening — it's the best spot for a breeze here.
pros: New, very clean, modern rooms; many have a kitchenette
Gym better than the price suggests + rooftop sky garden
Free train-station and airport shuttle, very convenient
Free underground parking · strong Wi-Fi throughout
cons: No pool, compact building, modest common areas
Uneven hot-water pressure in some rooms

entries.name: Surin Majestic Hotel
entries.badge: 🚌 By the bus terminal · has a pool
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chitbamrung Rd · next to the BKS bus terminal
tags: 🚌 Step off the coach into the lobby
entries.addr: 99 Chitbamrung Rd, Nai Mueang, Mueang Surin
entries.storyHtml: Surin Majestic Hotel is one of the handiest, best-value city hotels in town, sitting right beside the Surin BKS bus terminal — step off the coach and walk into the lobby, scoring 8.7 from 17 reviews. Its edge is an outdoor pool and gym, rare at this price point in Surin, plus a breakfast buffet many call better than the price. The City Pillar Shrine and in-town market are a few minutes' walk. The trade-off: the rooms lean classic/older in style, and the pool occasionally closes for maintenance over festivals.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room with a balcony over the pool — not every room has one, and it makes for a nicer outlook. If you're coming specifically to swim, call ahead, as the pool sometimes closes over festivals. Arriving by coach is easiest, since you walk straight off the bus into the hotel.
pros: Next to the bus terminal; walk to the shrine and market
Pool and gym, hard to find at this price in Surin
Breakfast buffet above the price, included in many rates
Free, generous parking · friendly staff
cons: Classic, older-style rooms; some furnishings show wear
Pool sometimes closed for maintenance over festivals — check first

entries.name: Destino Hotel Surin
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Surin–Sikhoraphum Rd · next to Robinson Surin
entries.addr: 444 Moo 16, Surin–Sikhoraphum Rd, Salakdai, Mueang Surin
entries.storyHtml: Destino Hotel Surin is a small, newly opened boutique of around 20 rooms sitting right beside Robinson Lifestyle Surin, scoring 8.8 from 11 reviews. Its strength is newness — everything still clean and modern, rare in a town where most stays are a fair age. Rooms are modern with comfy beds, some with a garden-view balcony; the made-to-order breakfast earns praise, and the mall is a short walk away. The trade-offs: no pool, it sits on a busy road with some traffic noise, and review numbers are still low as it's new.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: You can walk straight to Robinson for food and supplies without driving. Light sleeper? Ask for an inner room away from the main road to dodge traffic noise. Some rooms have a garden-view balcony — request one if you want a more open feel.
pros: New hotel, very clean rooms, everything still modern
Next to Robinson Surin, easy walk for shopping and food
Made-to-order breakfast, praised flavour · free
Free parking, free Wi-Fi, friendly staff
cons: On a busy road; some rooms catch traffic noise
No pool or spa · still few reviews as it's new

entries.name: S-House Hotel Surin
entries.revCount: Real reviews 8.8 · 56 reviews · cleanliness in the low 9s
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Salakdai · walk across the car park to Robinson
entries.storyHtml: S-House Hotel Surin is a budget hotel in a new building whose standout is cleanliness, scoring around 8.8 from 56 reviews with cleanliness up in the low 9s. The big draw is sitting right next to Robinson Lifestyle Surin — walk across the car park and you're at the mall, with restaurants, a supermarket and a cinema. The rooms genuinely look new, beds are comfy, parking is wide and free, and it's quiet (guests mention a resident cat). The trade-off: it's on the edge of town, not central, so without a car getting around is awkward, and rooms have no kettle or tea/coffee set.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Use the adjacent Robinson as your kitchen and supermarket — grab tea, coffee, water and snacks to bring back. Ask for a room in the new block, set back from the road, for the best condition and quiet. Weekend evening check-in can mean a short queue, as it gets busy.
pros: New, standout-clean rooms, comfy beds and pillows
Next to Robinson — walk across the car park to the mall
Wide free parking with an EV charger
Quiet and peaceful, great value at this price
cons: On the edge of town, not central; awkward without a car
No kettle or tea/coffee set in the rooms

entries.name: The Gun Hotel Premium
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Suriyakan Rd · around the monument & market
entries.addr: 13/1 Suriyakan Rd, Nai Mueang, Mueang Surin
entries.storyHtml: The Gun Hotel Premium is a small in-town hotel whose selling point is the rooms — big, clean, soft beds, and every room with a balcony and kitchenette, scoring 8.4 from 41 reviews. Rooms come with a fridge, microwave and kettle, handy for longer stays or heating your own food. It's in the monument/market area, about a 9-minute walk to the City Pillar Shrine and Wat Nong Bua, with free parking. Worth knowing: there's no lift, and no breakfast or pool — the 'Premium' name oversells it a little.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: There's no lift, so if you've got heavy bags or struggle with stairs, ask for a ground-floor room when booking. Make the most of the kitchenette — buy from the in-town market and heat it up in your room. No breakfast on site, but there are cafés and local restaurants within walking distance.
pros: Big, clean rooms with soft beds and pillows
Balcony and kitchenette in every room — fridge, microwave
Central, walk to the shrine, free parking
Friendly staff who speak Thai, English and Khmer
cons: No lift; upper-floor rooms mean carrying bags upstairs
No breakfast and no pool

entries.name: Sorin Boutique Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Thesaban 3 Rd · city centre · near market & monument
entries.addr: 22/88 Thesaban 3 Rd, Nai Mueang, Mueang Surin
entries.storyHtml: Sorin Boutique Hotel is a four-storey boutique where each guest floor is themed on something Surin is known for — silk, ancient Khmer temples and jasmine rice, scoring 8.4 from 39 reviews and ranked #2 in Surin's special-style category on TripAdvisor. Opened in 2019, the rooms are still new and modern, with a free minibar, free parking and an EV charger, plus a breakfast guests mention often. It's central, near the market and the monument. The trade-offs: no pool or spa, the walls between rooms are a bit thin, and it sits in a quiet soi where you'll drive out for late-night food.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For the full themed feel, ask at check-in which floor has which theme and pick one you like. Light sleeper? Request an upper floor or a corner room. Get to breakfast early (06:00–10:00) for the freshest hot dishes and the fullest spread.
pros: Surin-themed design with a real local feel in the décor
New, clean rooms, comfy beds, cold air-con, opened 2019
Free private parking with an EV charger
Thai and international breakfast · friendly staff
cons: Thin-ish walls between rooms · Wi-Fi patchy at times
No pool or spa · in a quiet soi, drive out for late-night food

entries.name: The Greenwich Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Yutthana Rd · suburb · road out to Huay Saneng
tags: 🚗 Park at your door + leafy garden
entries.addr: 50/2 Yutthana Rd, Nai Mueang, Mueang Surin
entries.storyHtml: The Greenwich Resort is a newly opened sub-฿1,000 stay whose strengths are clean rooms, quiet and parking right at your door, scoring 8.7 from 12 reviews. It's a small green-themed resort on Yutthana Road, on the suburban edge that's the route out to Huay Saneng reservoir. There are just 16 rooms, each 24 sqm, modern and well-equipped (smart TV, fridge, water heater), with a leafy garden and a large car park that takes coaches and vans. The trade-offs: the suburban location needs a car, there's no on-site restaurant, and review numbers are still low as it's new.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a small new place like this, contacting them directly via their page or Line often makes booking and pricing easier. It works best if you arrive by car, since you can park at your door. Coming as a group or using the garden for an event? Tell them ahead to reserve space and parking.
pros: Newly opened, clean rooms, modern green-themed design
Park at your door; large car park takes coaches/vans
Quiet, with a leafy garden to stroll
From a few hundred baht, good value for new rooms
cons: Suburban, awkward without a car · no on-site restaurant
Small, just 16 rooms, newly opened, few reviews so far

entries.name: Thong Tarin Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Sirirat Rd · city centre · near the monument
entries.addr: 60 Sirirat Rd, Nai Mueang, Mueang Surin
entries.storyHtml: Thong Tarin Hotel is the town stalwart locals name first — a 200-plus-room 4-star in the centre on Sirirat Road, scoring 8.3 from 52 reviews and #5 of 12 Surin hotels on TripAdvisor. It's not a new design boutique but a full-service hotel with a saltwater pool, several restaurants, and a banquet hall locals use for weddings. It's central, near the monument and market, with wide free parking. The trade-off: it opened in 2005 and only partly renovated, so room condition isn't consistent across the building.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for an upper-floor renovated room not above the banquet hall — comfier beds and quieter on event nights. If you'd rather avoid event noise, ask the front desk whether there's a wedding or seminar that night. There's wide free parking, so it works well as a base for exploring town.
pros: Central, near the monument, market and Surin Plaza
Saltwater pool, massage room and a classic marble lobby
Big banquet and meeting halls for weddings and seminars
Wide free parking · good value for a central 4-star
cons: Ageing building and décor; some rooms still older
Some noise on nights with a banquet event

entries.name: Surintara Resort
entries.badge: 🌳 Garden resort · park at your door
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Nok Mueang · near Huay Saneng reservoir
entries.storyHtml: Surintara Resort is a single-storey resort drivers love because you park right at your door, scoring 8.3 from 41 reviews. It's a 34-room 3-star in Nok Mueang sub-district, out near Huay Saneng reservoir — a popular sunset spot for locals. Rooms are big and clean, some with a sit-out balcony, set around a leafy garden with an on-site restaurant. The trade-offs: it's out of town, not walkable to the market or station so you'll need a car, and there's no pool.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Parking is right at each room, so you step from the car into your room — great for families on a road trip. In the evening, drive over to nearby Huay Saneng reservoir for the sunset. Ask for a room with a balcony when booking for the full resort feel.
pros: Single-storey resort, park at your door, easy for drivers
Rooms bigger than the price suggests, clean, comfy beds
Quiet, leafy garden setting near Huay Saneng
On-site restaurant · free Wi-Fi in all rooms · good value
cons: Out of town, needs a car, not walkable to the market
Budget resort: no pool or gym

entries.name: Maneerote Hotel Surin
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Krung Si Nai Rd · in town · walk to the train station
entries.addr: 11/1 Poi Tang Ko Soi, Krung Si Nai Rd, Nai Mueang, Mueang Surin
entries.storyHtml: Maneerote Hotel Surin is the cheapest stay in this guide from just ฿470, yet the rooms run a roomy 32 sqm and you can walk from the train station, scoring 8.2 from 52 reviews with cleanliness at 8.4. It's a value 3-star opened in 2010 on Poi Tang Ko Soi, central Surin. The standouts are spacious rooms with a long desk, high-speed Wi-Fi 6, and an in-house Muang Chang Coffee — good for remote workers and rail travellers. The trade-offs: no pool or gym, and hot water is fiddly to set in some rooms.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Step off at Surin station and walk over — no need for a ride, ideal if you're touring without a car. Working remotely? Tell staff you need the connection and you'll get a room with a strong signal. Try the in-house Muang Chang Coffee for breakfast and a coffee before heading out.
pros: Cheapest in the guide ฿470 · big 32 sqm rooms
Walk from Surin station, near the shrine and market
High-speed Wi-Fi 6, good for remote work
In-house café · free parking · 24-hour front desk
cons: Budget hotel: no pool or gym
Hot water fiddly to set in some rooms · no in-room safe

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Surin hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in around Surin?
faq.a: It depends on how you're travelling. The city centre (around the City Pillar Shrine, the monument and the in-town market) suits exploring temples and Isan food on foot (Hop Inn, The Wood, Slive, Sorin). Near the train and bus stations suits rail and coach travellers — step off and walk to your room (Maneerote, Surin Majestic). The Robinson side and out-of-town near Huay Saneng are quiet with easy parking, best for drivers (S-House, Destino, Surintara, The Greenwich).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Surin hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary: budget hotels and resorts start around ฿470–650/night (Maneerote, S-House, Surintara, The Greenwich, Hop Inn); mid-range and boutiques run about ฿800–1,300 (The Gun, The Wood, Slive, Sorin, Destino); central 4-stars run about ฿900–1,100 (Thong Tarin, Surin Majestic). All are approximate from-rates for standard rooms. During the Surin Elephant Round-up in November, rates run well above normal.

faq.q: ❓ Coming to Surin without a car — where's easiest?
faq.a: Surin has no metro, so without a car, staying in the city centre or near the train/bus station is easiest. Maneerote Hotel Surin ฿470 is a walk from the train station; Surin Majestic Hotel ฿1,100 is next to the BKS bus terminal — step off the coach into the lobby; Slive Hotel ฿1,000 runs a free 24-hour train-station shuttle. The Robinson, Huay Saneng and out-of-town stays suit drivers better.

faq.q: ❓ Visiting during the Surin Elephant Round-up — how far ahead to book?
faq.a: The Surin Elephant Round-up runs in mid-November each year — a big festival that draws crowds across the province. Hotels across town fill fast and rates rise sharply, so book weeks to a month ahead, especially central and station-area hotels. Pick a free-cancellation rate if your plans aren't set.

faq.q: ❓ Which Surin hotels have a pool?
faq.a: Pools are limited in Surin city. Surin Majestic Hotel ฿1,100 has an outdoor pool and gym, next to the bus terminal; Thong Tarin Hotel ฿900 has a saltwater pool and big banquet hall. Newer hotels like Slive have a gym and rooftop but no pool. If you're set on swimming, call the hotel first, as pools can close for maintenance over festivals.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Surin hotels?
faq.a: Prices differ across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com depending on each site's promotions, so open and compare all three before booking — every review page in this guide includes the comparison links. It can save hundreds of baht a night, especially during the Elephant Round-up when rates climb.
